title: AgentLens: Revealing The Lucky Pass Problem in SWE-Agent Evaluation
topic: Data-centric AI->Data-centric AI methods and tools
claim: Outcomes that look identical under binary evaluation actually spread across a wide range of process quality, revealing hidden weak successes.
layout: single histogram, left-to-right, shaded tier regions split by dashed threshold lines
description: A single histogram of per-trajectory quality scores (x-axis 0–100, y-axis Count up to about 140) drawn as light blue bars. The distribution is roughly bell-shaped and peaks around 60–68, with a long thin tail toward low scores. Two vertical dashed lines, red at about 47 and green at 70, split the plot into three tinted background regions: pink on the left for Lucky, pale orange in the middle for Solid, and pale green on the right for Ideal. Each region has a bold colored label at the top giving its count and percentage: Lucky 122 (10.7%), Solid 785 (69.1%), Ideal 229 (20.2%). The eye goes first to the colored labels and the tall central bars. The shading makes the tier boundaries clear.
caption: Passing trajectories are not behaviorally homogeneous. Among 1,136 passing trajectories in AGENTLENS- Bench, AGENTLENS classifies 229 as Ideal (20.2%), 785 as Solid (69.1%), and 122 as Lucky (10.7%). Binary evaluation treats all of these trajectories as equally successful, while process-aware scoring separates direct, coherent solutions from weak processes that happen to pass.
abstract: Evaluation of software engineering (SWE) agents is dominated by a binary signal: whether the final patch passes the tests. This outcome-only view treats a principled solution and a chaotic trial-and-error process as equivalent. We show that this equivalence is empirically false. We evaluate 2,614 OpenHands trajectories from eight model backends on 60 SWE-bench Verified tasks. Of these, 47 have enough passing trajectories to construct task-level process references, yielding a 1,815-trajectory evaluation subset. Among passing trajectories in this subset, 10.7% exhibit behavior we call a Lucky Pass: regression cycles, blind retries, missing verification, or temporally disordered exploration, implementation, and verification. We introduce AgentLens, a framework for process-level assessment of SWE-agent trajectories, and release AgentLens-Bench, a dataset of 1,815 trajectories annotated with quality scores, waste signals, divergence points, and 47 task-level Prefix Tree Acceptor (PTA) references. AgentLens builds PTA references by merging multiple passing solutions for the same task, and uses a context-sensitive intent labeler to assign actions to Exploration, Implementation, Verification, or Orchestration based on trajectory history rather than tool identity alone. On AgentLens-Bench, the quality score separates passing trajectories into Lucky, Solid, and Ideal tiers and further decomposes Lucky Passes into five recurring mechanisms. Across the eight model backends, Lucky rates range from 0.5% to 23.2%, and some models move by as many as five rank positions when ranked by quality score instead of pass rate. We publicly release AgentLens-Bench and the AgentLens SDK at https://github.com/agentlens-framework/agentlens, with a project page at https://agentlens-framework.github.io/agentlens/.
